steps.text: Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add beef and sauté until browned, about 5 minutes. Stir in garlic powder, salt, and pepper, then transfer mixture to a slow cooker.
Add a few tablespoons water to the skillet. Stir over medium heat, scraping up any browned bits with a spoon. Transfer liquid and browned bits to the slow cooker.
Add remaining water, broth, carrots, green onions, celery, barley, and parsley. Cover and cook on Low until vegetables and barley are tender, 6 to 8 hours.
Stir in thyme just before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker Beef Barley Soup
raw_recipe.description: This hearty beef barley soup is loaded with tender cubes of beef, colorful veggies, and fluffy barley in a rich broth for a nourishing winter meal.
raw_recipe.name: Slow Cooker Beef Barley Soup

review.reviewBody: My husband and I loved this soup. I did however make some minor changes. First, I added one beef soup bone, I find that this always helps add more flavor to any soup. Second I used 2 cups of water, 2 cups of beef broth, and 2 cups of chicken broth to balance the flavors. Also, I added fresh garlic instead of garlic powder. Last, I only used 1/2 a cup of barley and I added the barley 2hrs. before serving it. The first time I made this soup I added the barley in the beginning the barley ended up mushy.

I made this for dinner last night and it was great, except for one thing. When I browned the stew meat in the oil the recipe said "add a little water to the skillet and stir to pick up the browned bits." I did that but my soup turned out WAY too greasy, next time I would just use the meat!

This is a great starter recipe for Beef Barley Soup. I don't bother with the slow cooker; I do it right on my stovetop. I let it simmer on low for about 2 or 3 hours, and the beef comes out unbelievably tender. I also don't use the plain water at all. I use all beef broth to cook the veggies and the meat and it works so much better than just water. I also add balsamic vinegar and a touch of tomato paste to the meat to give some tanginess.

Many changes. 2 containers of broth Onions instead of green onions Season beef before browning 1 tsp minced garlic. 1 not 6 cups water 2 tbsp beef Boulion liquid. Result, richer flavour and deliciousness!
I covered the meat with flour before I cooked it. so, it was thicker, which my husbsnd liked

Made this for my husband and I and we enjoyed it. We didn't find it bland at all as others have posted. I followed the recipe very closely. I used a chuck roast that I cut up myself. Before sauteing, I generously seasoned the meat with salt, black pepper, garlic powder, and dried parsley. To the slow cooker, I added one clove of chopped garlic, along with a bit of salt and pepper. I used the called-for beef broth, but I added only 2 cups of water. I added the pearl barley with two hours left to the cooking time (six hours on low). The end result was a hearty, soup/stew with plenty of flavor.

This was delicious. I added three minced garlic cloves. I was out of beef broth so I used Beef Better Than Bouillon. I also added some frozen peas and corn that I needed to use up. I cooked it for 8 hours on low and added the barley two hours before it was done. It was even better the next day.

I had leftover roast that I had cut into chunks and froze along with the drippings..so I used this in place of the meat and some broth. Also added 4 cups of beef broth.(didn't add water). I used carrots celery a couple mushrooms and garlic. Added a bay leaf, dried thyme and lots of pepper . I love the idea of the barley cooking in the slow cooker.. so convenient.

This is a decent base recipe. I have a smaller slow cooker than what this recipe was intended for so I couldn't use the recommended amount of liquid. I used around 3 stalks of celery because 4 seemed overkill. I would use all beef broth or a combo of beef & chicken broth next time as the water leaves it too flavorless. Aside from that, I added in 2 cans of diced potatoes, 2 cans of green beans, and 2 cans of peas. I used 2 lbs of cube steak and it was the perfect amount of meat. I was trying to replicate that Campbell's beef vegetable soup. This was very close. The only issue I had was that it seems to lack a true savory flavor, other wise it was good. Also, I used Pearl Barley and let it cook for 6-7 hours and it turned out fine, not mushy at all. It seems like the fast cooking barley many other use requires you to add it in last minute.

I made this today adding fresh sweet onion and two garlic cloves. This came out very tasty. I also added mushrooms at the last hour. 8 hours on low. Browned both cubed beef and beef short ribs. The short ribs were a bit greasy so I think next time I will not add as many. I only added beef broth and left the water out so it was more stew like. I did not add the thyme - I forgot. I will be making this again.

This is the first time I've event made barley soup but I did change the recipe. I used 2- 32oz. boxes of beef broth and reduced the water to 2 cups. Instead of the celery, onion and carrots, I added 2 small bags of frozen mixed vegetables and 3 leeks. For the cooking temperature / time, I cooked it on high for the first 3 hours and then reduced it to low until the barley and leeks were tender. It is fabulous!!

We tried it with raw chuck that was pan seared which made it a little more bland than intended. I also put small potatoes and carrots into it which needed to cook way longer than the barley needed so it came out like savory oatmeal. It was promising and still tasted pretty good but the texture was not good. If you try to put veggies into it then the barley needs to go in for only the last 2 or 3 hours.
Changed water to chicken broth & beef broth to chicken broth & beef buillion cube. Advice: don't put more barley than what's in recipe!

I made it with a good quality lean venison instead of beef and it was very good. Prefer a bit of tomato , beans, and corn with my beef barley. Added a pint of home-canned stewed tomatoes, some extra beef broth and about 1/2 cup extra barley, too. I used low salt beef broth and just had it on low in Crockpot overnight. Added as much 1 tsp of salt as the recipe calls for but ended up adding extra water in early morning, as it cooked down and was perfect for most people but too salty for my tastes.
This is my go-to recipe for beef broth soup. Perfect every time. I also add diced tomatoes for added flavour and zest.

I cut recipe in half and omitted the water substituting with beef broth. used all of the other instructions as writened with only 1/2 cup of barly, this soup fit into my 4qt crockpot. It was verey bland, will not be making again.
Adding tomato paste or crushed tomatoes really give the broth a nice rich flavour! Great recipe
Do it 4 hours on high

I used more broth and less water, white onion instead of green, and real garlic instead of powdered. I added the thyme at the start to better absorb the flavor and sautéed the onion and garlic a bit before adding. Even with that it was really bland. So when it was done I added more salt, some garlic powder, and allspice. That helped a lot and we enjoyed it.
Really lacking in flavor.
